image_description: A close-up, high-angle view of a Nile crocodile resting on a concrete or stone bank next to water. The image focuses heavily on the dorsal surface, showing the textured, armored skin (scutes) and the muscular tail extending towards the bottom left. The head is partially visible in the upper right, with one eye clearly seen. A small bird is perched on the crocodile's back near the neck.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the head shows a tapering snout consistent with a crocodilian V-shape, distinct from the broader U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the angle/occlusion prevents a clear view of the tooth interlock pattern or the specific 'fourth tooth' notch.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One eye is clearly visible, positioned on top of the head. While pupil shape is hard to resolve at this resolution, the dorsal positioning is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is either out of frame or obscured by the angle and lighting, making nostril verification impossible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays an elongated body covered in heavy, bony armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal scutes are prominent, forming distinct longitudinal ridges and rows, matching the taxonomic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of muddy yellow/brown and dark grey/black on the ridges, with a visibly rough texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodile is viewed from above; the belly (ventral side) is completely occluded by the body and the ground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a small portion of one hind limb is visible at the very edge of the frame; digits and webbing cannot be counted or verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is prominently featured, showing significant musculature and lateral compression (height > width) typical of aquatic propulsion.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The very end of the tail appears slightly 'mushy' or smoothed out compared to the sharp definition of the scutes further up the body. It lacks the distinct terminal spike detail often seen, blending slightly into the background.

artifact_observations.location: Junction of tail and ground (bottom center)
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight ambiguity in the contact shadow where the tail meets the stone edge. The boundary is soft, suggesting minor depth estimation issues or edge bleeding, though not catastrophic.

The bird is present but lacks fine feather detail, appearing somewhat 'painted on' or low-resolution compared to the crocodile skin. This is common in AI generation where secondary subjects lose fidelity.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification of species-specific features (scute pattern, snout shape) against ImageNet classes.
To verify the continuity of the scutes and ensure no 'melting' occurs between the armored plates, especially along the tail ridge.
To assess the physical grounding of the heavy reptile on the stone surface and check for floating artifacts or incorrect contact shadows.
To evaluate the texture consistency of the skin vs. the bird and the water, checking for subtle generative blur or noise inconsistencies.

focus_areas: Continuity and realism of dorsal scutes (osteoderms)
Structural integrity of the tail tip
Contact shadows between crocodile and stone bank
Anatomical correctness of the visible eye and snout shape
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the crocodile's skin and the background. AI models often struggle with the complex, high-frequency texture of crocodile scales, leading to 'smearing' or repetitive patterns. Verify if the scute arrangement follows biological logic (longitudinal rows) or if it becomes chaotic/nonsensical towards the tail. Also, assess if the bird is structurally plausible or just a texture blob.
